transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Do you have any questions for me today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi, yes, I do have some questions. Firstly, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for about a month. So gentle gardening is fine, but take it easy and don't overdo it.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the information. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using it unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

However, I don't have specific information about when to start using it after surgery if you weren't using it before. I'd recommend checking with your care team about that, or you could speak to your GP or pharmacist for guidance.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, please let your care team know.

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good. However, if the light sensitivity is severe or your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further.

For mild sensitivity, we'd recommend just wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, just one more. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

However, I don't know exactly how long it's been since your operation. If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all my questions for now. Thank you so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, you've answered all my questions. Thanks again!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Excellent! I'm glad I could help. Take care and best wishes with your recovery!
